reason: The text emphasizes hierarchy through multiple dimensions: (1) Explicit social hierarchy—Job is explicitly described as 'greater than all the people of the east' (gadol mikkal benei kedem), establishing clear superiority; (2) Familial hierarchy—Job is positioned as undisputed head of household with authority over his children and extensive servants ('avudah rabah meod'); (3) Cosmic hierarchy—the passage depicts a clear celestial order with God at the apex, the 'Sons of God' (benei ha-Elohim) subordinate to Him, and Satan subject to God's authority and limitations; (4) Patriarchal responsibility—Job exercises priestly authority over his children, sanctifying them and making intercessions on their behalf. The hierarchical structure is presented not as problematic but as integral to the ordered world and to Job's righteous and blessed condition. Prosperity and authority are interrelated as blessings in the text's framework.
